"Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low." In the macro-finance literature, sustained employment gains strengthen household and firm balance sheets and reduce the impact of adverse net-worth shocks (the financial accelerator mechanism highlighted by Bernanke and Gertler), supporting aggregate demand through the IS curve. With sticky prices, monetary policy primarily influences real activity in the short run (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans; Nakamura and Steinsson), so strong labor-market conditions typically map into continued output expansion without immediate, outsized inflation pressure—especially when market- and survey-based inflation expectations are anchored below target (Svensson and Woodford’s inflation-forecast-targeting perspective). These features justify the FOMC’s modestly accommodative stance despite low unemployment, reinforcing a moderately positive tone for growth, albeit tempered by soft business investment noted elsewhere in the statement.
